official.deadline_note: The 2026 round closed on 2 March 2026 at 14:00 CET. The University of Vienna runs a central doctoral call each year, but no dates for the next round were published on the official careers site as of 10 October 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2026 cycle: applications 7 January to 2 March 2026, 14:00 CET; employment start between 1 July and 1 October 2026. Next cycle expected but not yet announced.
official.status_note: The official page states: 'The application deadline was 2 March, 14:00 CET' and directs candidates to the Application Portal. The University of Vienna announces new central doctoral calls each year (a separate Autumn Call for 11 PhD positions opens September 2026), but no new SSH call window had been published as of 10 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No, employees of the University of Vienna are exempt from tuition fees. Please note: You have to pay the Students Union fee (currently EUR 25.20) each semester. Otherwise, your admission expires automatically.
official.funding_period: per month gross, paid 14 times per year
benefits: Monthly gross salary of EUR 2,786.10 in salary group B1 for a workload of 30 hours per week, paid 14 times per year
Exemption from tuition fees for University of Vienna employees
Comprehensive social security coverage, including health insurance (also covering family members and unemployed partners), pension contributions, and unemployment insurance
Entitlement to parental leave in accordance with Austrian employment law
The collective bargaining agreement also includes the possibility of teaching
eligibility: Highly qualified graduate who will have completed a Diploma or Master's degree by 30 June 2026 in a field covered by one of the participating doctoral schools or a closely related discipline
Demonstrates a strong interest in academic research and in pursuing a PhD at the University of Vienna
Can clearly assign the proposed dissertation project to the research focus of one of the participating doctoral schools
Able to take up the doctoral position between 1 July and 1 October 2026
Meets the doctoral admission requirements of the University of Vienna by the start of employment
Already enrolled applicants are eligible if their first doctoral enrolment at the University of Vienna was in winter semester 2025/26 or later
Applicants with foreign degrees are welcome
requirements: A separate CV is not required, as all relevant information is captured in the structured fields of the online application form
Only one application may be submitted; if more are submitted, only the last one is considered
No confirmation of supervision is required at the application stage, and applicants are asked not to contact supervisors before applying
Applicants who already hold external funding for the doctoral project or an existing praedoc-level employment contract of at least two years cannot receive funding through this call
Non-EU/EEA applicants must obtain the required visa or work permit themselves; the University provides supporting documentation
Funding through the call cannot be extended beyond four years
documents: Completed online application form (no separate CV)
Research proposal of a maximum of 5 pages including bibliography (PDF)

Master, Bachelor and/or Diploma degree certificates and transcript of records or diploma supplements (PDF); an official confirmation of expected completion by June 2026 is accepted in place of a missing diploma
Official identification document, passport or ID card, for enrolment (PDF)
If applicable and available: residence permit and language certificate(s) (PDF)
Writing sample (e.g. a chapter of the Master's thesis or a published article) for applicants to Ars Iuris Vienna, DSE, DSHCS, VDP, VDTR and VISESS (PDF)
Contact details of two referees; no letters of recommendation are submitted at the application stage
selection_criteria: Academic achievements and previous research experience
Quality, originality and feasibility of the research proposal
Fit between the project and the doctoral school environment and potential supervisors
Online interviews between late March and mid-May 2026 explore motivation, research potential and alignment
A ranked waiting list is created; offers must be accepted within 2 weeks
coverage: Salaried employment of 30 hours per week for four years under collective bargaining agreement para. 48 VwGr. B1
Monthly gross salary of EUR 2,786.10, paid 14 times per year
Exemption from University of Vienna tuition fees (Employees still pay the Students Union fee of EUR 25.20 per semester)
Comprehensive social security coverage including health insurance for family members and unemployed partners, pension and unemployment insurance
application_method: Central online application through the University of Vienna PhD Selection Tool
Registration for a u:account is required first if the applicant does not already have one
The form can be saved and edited until finally submitted; applications remain editable until the deadline
official.application_route: One central online application via the University of Vienna PhD Selection Tool (u:account first), with all PDFs uploaded in the form before the deadline.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international applicants with degrees from foreign universities are welcome, provided they meet the doctoral admission requirements of the University of Vienna.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The proposed dissertation project must be assignable to the research focus of one of the nine participating doctoral schools (Ars Iuris Vienna, PhilKult, CoBeNe, DSE, DSHCS, VDP, ViDSS, VDTR, VISESS); applicants with related or interdisciplinary backgrounds are eligible if both degree and project fit a doctoral school.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal of at most 5 pages including bibliography, containing a project summary with research questions, state of the art, theoretical/methodological approach and relevant literature.
official.description: The University of Vienna invites applications for at least 40 fully funded, 4-year doctoral positions in the social sciences, humanities and cultural studies across nine participating doctoral schools. Positions are contracted for 30 hours per week under collective bargaining agreement para. 48 VwGr. B1 at a monthly gross salary of EUR 2,786.10 paid 14 times per year, and employees are exempt from tuition fees.
official.program_type: Central annual recruitment call for salaried predoctoral (Praedoc) positions at a doctoral school
official.english_requirement: All doctoral schools accept applications in English, and five additionally accept German. Admission to the doctoral programme usually requires language proficiency in German and/or English corresponding to level C1; for most subjects language certificates are not mandatory but any available certificate should be provided, and pre-selected candidates prove their competences in the interview phase.

verification.notes: Salary (EUR 2,786.10 gross, salary group B1, 30h/week, 14 payments per year), tuition exemption incl. EUR 25.20 Students Union fee, eligibility, documents, selection timeline and the closed 2 March 2026 deadline were verified on the official University of Vienna careers pages; the next round's dates are not yet published.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a salaried four-year employment contract at the University of Vienna, not a stipend, so you receive full social security and pay no tuition - only the EUR 25.20 Students Union fee per semester. The 2026 round closed on 2 March 2026; the University runs the call annually, so monitor careers.univie.ac.at/en/praedoc from around January for the next window and prepare your materials in advance. Plan the application so you can realistically complete your Master's degree by the end of June of the intake year and start between July and 1 October.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong final-year Master's/Diploma graduates in SSH fields whose project maps cleanly onto one of the nine doctoral schools and who want a salaried, social-secured PhD in Vienna.
application_readiness_checklist: Map your project to exactly one of the nine doctoral schools before drafting anything; the fit is assessed explicitly
Draft the research proposal to a strict 5-page limit including bibliography, with research questions, state of the art, method and timeline
If your diploma is not yet issued, request an official confirmation from your university stating all requirements will be completed by the end of June
Register your u:account early and complete the PhD Selection Tool form fields rather than a CV
Collect contact details of two referees; they are only contacted later, if at all
Check whether your target school is one of the six requiring a writing sample (Ars Iuris, DSE, DSHCS, VDP, VDTR, VISESS) and prepare a thesis chapter or publication
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that cannot be assigned to one participating doctoral school or that overlaps another applicant's external funding situation
Holding external project funding or a praedoc contract of two years or more, which rules out funding through this call
Missing Master's degree components (grading or thesis defence) still outstanding at the end of June
Submitting multiple applications - only the last one counts, so a stray duplicate can overwrite your intended submission
Contacting supervisors for confirmation before applying, which the FAQ explicitly asks applicants not to do
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Vienna living costs beyond the gross salary (which is taxed and social-security deducted), the EUR 25.20 Students Union fee per semester, any travel to Austria, and any conference or research costs - additional funding or travel support must be negotiated with your institute and supervisor after employment starts.
document_audit: Degree certificates plus transcripts/diploma supplements must be complete PDFs; a completion confirmation letter is only a substitute until the diploma exists
The passport or ID card upload is for enrolment, so it must be current and match your legal name
The writing sample requirement differs by doctoral school - double-check the six-school list before uploading
The research proposal has a hard 5-page cap including bibliography, so bibliography length eats into your content budget
alerts: The window is short (historically 7 January to early March) and technical problems on the last day are not excused - submit early
Non-EU/EEA applicants must arrange their own visa or work permit; the University only supplies documents
Offers must be accepted within two weeks and a ranked waiting list exists, so declines move quickly
Funding cannot be extended beyond four years through this call; later funding must be sought elsewhere
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register a u:account, complete and save the PhD Selection Tool form (editable until the deadline), upload all PDFs, receive an automatic confirmation email, then await the March eligibility check, online interviews late March to mid-May, and decisions by June.

official.deadline_note: Closing date published as 01.12.2026 on grants.at and as December 1st, 2026, 23:59 CET in the official FAQ; online application is possible from September onwards for stays during the academic year 2027/28.
official.application_cycle: 2027/28 cycle - online application open from September 2026, closing 1 December 2026, for research stays during the Austrian academic year 2027/28 (earliest start September 2027); results expected at the beginning of July 2027.
official.status_note: Online application is possible from September to December 1st for stays during the Austrian academic year 2027/28; the earliest start is September 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Grant holders do not have to pay tuition fees in Austria. Tuition fees may be waived upon request to the Rectorate of the public university or university college for teacher education for the semesters in which studies or research can be shown to have been completed elsewhere. Any tuition fees at universities of applied sciences may be waived by the rectorate upon application. This does not apply to tuition fees at private universities and private colleges.
benefits: Monthly grant rate: 1,300 Euro (supplementary grant, own funds are required)
Assistance in arranging accommodation (OeAD student housing may be applied for; availability is limited and a room cannot be guaranteed)
Assistance in taking out health insurance accepted by the Austrian authorities (holders pay the insurance themselves; roughly EUR 55 to 200 per month)

Travel costs subsidy of up to 1,200 Euro upon submission of original travel invoices for scholarship holders with citizenship and travel from non-European developing countries (LDCs, Low Income and Lower Middle Income Countries and Territories on the DAC list, plus Gabon, Malaysia, Namibia, South Africa, Thailand)
eligibility: Postgraduates pursuing a doctoral/PhD programme outside Austria
Postgraduates and postdocs wishing to pursue research in Austria with a view to an academic career who completed their studies at a university outside Austria after 30 September 2025
Postdocs who are working as lecturers or researchers at a university outside Austria
Applicants must not have lived/studied/pursued research/pursued academic work in Austria in the last six months before taking up the grant
Applicants who completed their academic education mainly in Austria (except postdocs) or are already permanently residing in Austria are not eligible
Maximum age: 35 years (born on or after 01 October 1991)
Country of origin: all countries except Austria
Language skills: very good knowledge of English and/or German
The scholarship is only granted for projects that can be completed within the scholarship period (max. 9 months)
requirements: Documents have to be uploaded with the online application at www.scholarships.at; nothing arriving after the deadline is accepted
The use of generative AI must be indicated in the application
Applicants seeking admission to a university in Austria have to contact the institution directly
Grant holders must be continuously present at their place of study in Austria to conduct the research project

Gainful employment is not allowed; exempt is marginal employment within research/the Arts at universities, universities of applied sciences and research institutions in compliance with residence and employment laws (in 2026: EUR 551.10 per month)
The grant has to be consumed by the end of 2028
Scholarship holders are obliged to submit a final report at the end of their scholarship stay
Written confirmation of supervision from a lecturer at the Austrian target university is a required document
It is strongly recommended to take out adequate health, accident and repatriation insurance; the scholarship holder is responsible for insurance
documents: Two letters of recommendation by university lecturers, freely worded but with letterhead, date, signature and the stamp of the university/department, not older than six months at the time of application
Consent of a lecturer at the Austrian target university to supervise the applicant academically, using the OeAD template with date, signature and stamp
Scanned copy of a valid biometric passport (page with name and photo); an identity card is only acceptable for applications from the EU
Scanned copy of the university graduation certificate of diploma, master, PhD or doctoral studies
Only for PhD students: confirmation of participation in a PhD programme at the home university
Only for postdocs: confirmation of employment at the home university
Documents neither in English nor German: upload the original plus a rough English or German translation (certified translation not required)
selection_criteria: Examination of the formal requirements; incomplete or non-compliant applications are rejected before further selection
Examination of the application's general plausibility
Assessment and evaluation of the application by experts from the respective field
Final decision by the BMFWF; selection is competitive with no legal claim, and the number of grants depends on quota and budget
coverage: Supplementary grant with monthly grant rate of 1,300 Euro; own funds are required because actual living costs in Austria are assumed to be higher than the grant
Assistance in arranging accommodation and health insurance, whose costs scholarship holders pay themselves
Tuition fees: grant holders do not have to pay tuition fees in Austria; waiver upon request to the rectorate as published (not applicable to private universities and private colleges)
Travel costs subsidy of up to 1,200 Euro on original invoices for the listed non-European developing countries
Not covered: accommodation, compulsory health insurance (EUR 55-200 per month), travel to Austria, deposits and any costs above the grant rate
application_method: Online application at www.scholarships.at with all documents uploaded; no separate research proposal upload is needed - the structured sections of the form must describe the planned research (observe the minimum number of words/characters)
official.application_route: One online application via www.scholarships.at (portal opens September), uploading supervision confirmation, two stamped recommendation letters, passport and degree documents before 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET.
official.study_mode: Full-time research presence required; grant holders must be continuously present at the Austrian host institution, and stay periods must consist of full months starting on the first and ending on the last of a month.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants from all countries except Austria; applicants who completed their academic education mainly in Austria (does not apply to postdocs) or are permanently resident in Austria are not eligible, and no stay in Austria may have occurred in the six months before the grant starts.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - this is an incoming grant for young researchers from all countries except Austria.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All disciplines are eligible; any Austrian university can act as host, while non-university research institutes are assessed case by case by the OeAD (supervision must come from a supervisor who works at the institute and teaches at a university).
official.research_requirement: A research project that can be completed within the scholarship period (max. 9 months), described in the structured fields of the online application; written supervision confirmation from an Austrian university lecturer is mandatory.
official.description: The Ernst Mach Grant worldwide funds short research stays in Austria for young researchers of all disciplines and all countries except Austria, paying a monthly grant of EUR 1,300 for stays of 1 to 9 months during the academic year 2027/28. The OeAD describes the grant as supplementary and states that own funds are required, since actual living costs in Austria exceed the grant rate.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (incoming research grant financed by the BMFWF, awarded by OeAD-GmbH)
official.english_requirement: Very good knowledge of English and/or German. No official testing certificate such as TOEFL is needed, but applicants should have sufficient knowledge of English in the respective subject area, and the Austrian academic supervisor must confirm that the project can be done in English.

verification.notes: The grants.at detail page (awarding organisation OeAD-GmbH, last update 27.07.2026) confirms the EUR 1,300 monthly grant rate, the supplementary-grant and own-funds wording, tuition-fee treatment, the up-to-EUR 1,200 travel subsidy for DAC-list countries, the 01.12.2026 closing date, documents, eligibility and the 2026 marginal-employment limit of EUR 551.10; the official FAQ confirms the 2027/28 cycle, 1 December 2026 23:59 CET deadline, earliest start September 2027 and results at the beginning of July 2027.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a small, explicitly supplementary grant of EUR 1,300 per month for a 1-9 month research stay in Austria, and the OeAD states plainly that own funds are required because real Austrian living costs exceed the rate - budget for accommodation, insurance and deposits before applying. The current window is open now and closes 1 December 2026 for stays in the 2027/28 academic year, with the earliest start September 2027 and results only in early July 2027, leaving a tight runway for non-EU visa applicants. Only nationals of listed non-European developing countries (DAC list plus Gabon, Malaysia, Namibia, South Africa, Thailand) receive the travel subsidy of up to EUR 1,200, so applicants from anywhere else should treat travel to Austria as fully self-funded.
applicant_utility.best_fit: PhD candidates enrolled outside Austria, recent foreign graduates (after 30 September 2025) or postdocs aged 35 or under who have a concrete, short research question and an Austrian supervisor already willing to host them.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the written supervision confirmation on the OeAD template (signed, dated, stamped) before anything else - no supervisor means no valid application
Commission two recommendation letters from university lecturers with letterhead, date, signature and university/department stamp, dated within six months of submission
Confirm the age rule (born on or after 01 October 1991) and that at least six months have passed since any study, research or work stay in Austria
Scope the project so it is completable within the scholarship period of at most 9 months
Choose full-month stay dates (first of a month to last of a month); short 1-month stays should be planned for February or September to ease housing
Draft the form sections carefully - there is no proposal upload, and missing minimum word counts makes an application formally invalid
common_rejection_risks: Recommendation or supervision letters older than six months, or missing the university/department stamp
The Austrian supervisor also signing a recommendation letter - such a letter is treated as invalid
Non-certified digital signatures on letters where authenticity cannot be verified, rendering the application formally invalid
An application rejected as incomplete because form fields fall short of the minimum number of characters or insufficiently describe the research stay
Documents uploaded after the 1 December 2026 deadline are never accepted, and technical support is unavailable outside office hours at the last minute
Using the grant to enter a Master's or PhD programme in Austria, which is not permitted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation in Vienna (relevant to residence funds if above EUR 386.43 per month), compulsory health insurance (about EUR 55-200 per month depending on age and health), possible accommodation deposits, travel to and from Austria unless covered by the DAC-country subsidy, and any family or above-rate living costs the grant does not match.
document_audit: Passport must be a valid biometric passport uploaded as a scan; an identity card works only for EU applicants
The supervision confirmation must use the OeAD template with stamp, date and signature - a free-text email from a professor is not enough
Letters of recommendation must be on genuine university letterhead with a genuine stamp; copied or digitally inserted signatures fail the authenticity check
Foreign-language diplomas or employment confirmations need both the original scan and a rough English or German translation, but not a certified one
PhD students need proof of enrolment in the home programme; postdocs need proof of employment - one of the two, depending on your track
alerts: Results arrive only at the beginning of July 2027 for a September 2027 earliest start; non-EU applicants planning stays over 6 months should not rely on the earliest date because visa processing takes months

Non-EU/EEA applicants staying more than 6 months with accommodation costs above EUR 386.43 per month may need to prove additional funds to the Austrian residence authority, and a written accommodation proof is needed for the residence permit
No gainful employment during the grant, except marginal employment within research/the Arts capped at EUR 551.10 per month in 2026
The grant must be consumed by the end of 2028 and a final report is obligatory at the end of the stay
AI use in preparing the application must be declared, naming the tools and the extent of use
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create and complete the application online at www.scholarships.at (opening in September), upload supervision confirmation, two stamped letters, passport, degree and enrolment/employment documents, and submit by 1 December 2026 23:59 CET; OeAD then runs a formal check, a plausibility check and expert evaluation, with the final decision by the BMFWF and results published at the beginning of July 2027.
